content:
404 Media previously reported that iCloud+'s "Hide My Email" feature had a vulnerability that allowed anyone to obtain the user's real email address. Apple has now stated that the vulnerability has been officially fixed.

Apple stated that the security vulnerability in "Hide My Email" was patched earlier this month.

If you're subscribed to iCloud+ or Apple One, Apple's "Hide My Email" privacy feature is particularly useful for protecting your real email address.

According to Apple's website, here's how the feature works:

However, according to 404 Media's earlier report, "Hide My Email" had long contained a vulnerability that allowed anyone to obtain the real email address linked to an Apple account. This disclosure has prompted a new proposed lawsuit.

However, Apple stated today that the vulnerability was officially fixed earlier this month.

Apple told 404 Media that it had "deployed a fix for this issue on July 3, and the company said it has been completely resolved."

The iCloud+ vulnerability was first reported to Apple by Tyler Murphy in June 2025. After initial communication, Apple claimed it had been patched, but Murphy discovered the issue persisted. Hopefully this time it's truly resolved.

How often do you use the "Hide My Email" feature on iCloud+? Feel free to share in the comments section.
